title: An AI ‘reality check’ may take the S&P 500 to 5,000. Here are the trades to make, this strategist says.
source_used: Reuters flash on Devdiscourse (syndicated feed copy); Reuters market wrap on AOL.com for Monday's S&P 500 close. MarketWatch original not opened (HTTP 401); Investing.com copy of the Reuters story blocked (403).
key_facts: Panmure Liberum expects the S&P 500 to fall to 5,000 points by the end of 2027.
It warns that the market's resilience could unravel if bond yields and interest rates continue to rise.
Panmure said in a Monday (5 Oct 2026) note: 'We think the end of the equity bull market may be closer than many investors think.'
Reuters market wrap: the S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,773.95, so 5,000 would be a fall of about 36% (our arithmetic).
The Reuters headline: 'Panmure Liberum forecasts S&P 500 falling to 5,000, warns bull run nearing end'.
quote_evidence: Panmure Liberum expects the benchmark S&P 500 index to fall to 5,000 points by the end of 2027, warning that the market's resilience could unravel if bond yields and interest rates continue to rise.
"We think the end of the equity bull market may be closer than many investors think," Panmure said in a note on Monday.
The S&P 500 climbed 0.66% to end the session at 7,773.95 points.
why_it_matters_hint: A bold year-end 2027 forecast from one firm adds to the debate over whether AI-led gains and rising bond yields can coexist.
notes: MarketWatch page blocked (HTTP 401); its 'trades to make' angle was not read. Presumed to cover the same Panmure Liberum note (same 5,000 target, same day), which is not confirmed. Only a two-sentence Reuters flash was readable (Devdiscourse feed copy). 'Investment bank' for Panmure Liberum is general background; the feed text gives no description. The 36% figure is our own arithmetic from 5,000 and Monday's close.
